text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA
- Belgrade's Agrobanka to start selling hard currency on Wedenesday and other banks by the end of the week. Each citizen can buy foreign currency to the equivalent of 1,000 German marks a year.
- During his visit to Podgorica U.S. envoy Robert Gelbard expressed concern that many issues are not being resolved in Yugoslavia which are a condition for lifting of the outer wall of sanctions.
- Serbian parliament adopted in principle the law on local self-government. Councillors will be elected by majority electoral system in one electoral round.
- Yugoslav Interior Minister Zoran Sokolovic denied Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic was held up at Belgrade airport on Sunday.

- Official Macedonian delegation led by Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski is arriving on a two-day visit to Belgrade during which agreements on education and scientific technical cooperation are expected to be signed.

- "I beleive the Serbian Renewal Movement has broken coalition Zajedno with the aim of blocking the Democratic Party (DS)," said Vesna Pesic the head of the Civic Alliance of Serbia, the third coalition partner.

- Electricity company Serbia (EPS) and Czech bank expected to sign by end of the week an agreement on financing Czech concern Skoda Plzen for supplying equipment for the construction of Yugoslav thermo-electric power plant Kolubara B. The first tranche of the credit is expected to be $62 million.
- Foreign oil companies such as Shell and Texaco are interested in cooperation with the Serbian oil company NIS and are negotiting possible deals.
- The list of firms to be privatised under a special government programme will be issued in November.

- Basketball fans broke window panes on Croatian embassy in Belgrade during celebration of Yugoslavia's victory in a European basketball championship match against Croatia played in Spain. Croatia addresses protest note to Yugoslav foreign ministry.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav Trade Minister Borislav Vukovic is visiting Moscow to discuss promotion of bilateral cooperation and trade and financial cooperation agreements.
- The Serbian government soon to set up a directorate for development of undeveloped areas to be based in Pristina.
- Vojvodina will offer over 1.67 million tonnes of wheat on the market this year, over two thirds of which will be for export.
- Trial of fifteen Kosovo Albanians accused of terrorist activity will continue in Pristina on July 9 after being suspended because of medical tests of the chief defendant Besim Rama.
- Body of taxi driver found in car trunk. This is the fifth taxi driver to be killed in Belgrade in two years.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Bosnian Serb police are unified and determined to respect the state's constitutional order and legality, says Bosnian Serb interior minister Dragan Kijac.
BORBA

- Yugoslav committee for cooperation with United Nations peace missions and international forces condemned arrest of former Vukovar mayor Slavko Dokmanovic and said it would negatively affect the stay of Serbs in the region.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA
- Special U.S. envoy Robert Gelbard visited Montenegro and held separate talks with Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic, Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic and opposition leaders.

- Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic left for Moscow Tuesday evening where he is due to meet among others Moscow mayor Yuri Luskov, Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeni Primakov and the Russian Patriarch Alexei II.

- The situation in the republic's power system is alarming according to the Montenegrin power industry Elektroprivreda Crne Gore. Montenegro will have to import 80 million KWh of electricity in July worth 2.27 million dollars. If the government and the three biggest consumers do not provide hard currency the company will have to resort to power cuts.
- The Montenegrin parliament adopted a recommendation on registration of property of public officials when they take office. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311-4305
